_comment: The bus, with people in it. Run WINDOWED -- --headless disables rendering: godot --path . --run-shots art/shots_bus.json. The question these framings exist to answer is whether a rider reads as being IN the bus rather than balanced on a plank, so every shot has riders aboard and none of them is a beauty shot of an empty vehicle.

scenes.name: bus_three_quarter
scenes._comment: The everyday view: roughly where the game camera sits, close enough that the sides and the floor stripe are legible against the riders.

scenes.name: bus_side_on
scenes._comment: Square to the flank, which is the only framing where the stripe, the hubcaps and how far up a rider the sides come can all be judged at once. A three-quarter view foreshortens exactly the thing under review.

scenes.name: bus_nose_on
scenes._comment: Down the barrel of the front end, for the headlights and the radiator -- the parts a side view cannot show at all.
